chunks: Hariz narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Do not go out on the Day of al-Fitr until you eat something, and do not eat anything on the Day of al-Adha except from your sacrificial offering and your udhiyah, if you are able to do so. If you are not able, then you are excused.

He said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام also said, 'Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام would not eat anything on the Day of al-Adha until he ate from his udhiyah, and he would not go out on the Day of al-Fitr until he had eaten and given the fitrah.' Then he said, 'And likewise are we.'

key_terms.أُضْحِيَّتِكَ: your udhiyah, the animal you sacrifice
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Adha, the festival associated with sacrifice
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةَ: zakat al-fitr given before the Eid prayer
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr, the festival marking the end of fasting
key_terms.مَعْذُورٌ: excused when unable to perform the stated act

ai.seo_question: What should a person do before going out for Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives etiquette and rulings connected to the two Eid days. It instructs eating before going out on Eid al-Fitr, and delaying eating on Eid al-Adha until eating from one's sacrifice if able, while also presenting this as the practice of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
